title: Let support read permit codes out loud

blocks.text: This continues the parking permits of the previous practice: `Permits` now starts from its solution, and every permit also has a code printed on it. Residents read the code out to support on the phone, and support finds the car with `carWithPermit(...)`. Until now a code was compared the way a plate is, so `codeKey` simply returned `plateKey(code)`.

Support has a request. Codes are printed in a font where O and 0, and I and 1, look alike, and residents read them either way. Codes are never issued with the letters O or I, so in a code, an O always means 0 and an I always means 1. Plates are different: `LO-404-D` and `L0-404-D` are two cars, and both exist.

Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Permits.java`, `codeKey(...)`, and change anything else in the file you need to. When you're done, support finds the car from a code however the resident reads it out, and every car keeps its own permit. About two lines in total.

cases.says: a code read out exactly as printed finds the car its permit is on, also after a transfer
plates that differ only in O against 0 or I against 1 remain two cars, each with its own permit
a code read out with spaces or dashes and with O for 0 or I for 1 finds its car
a code typed in lower case with o for 0 and i for 1 finds its car

origin.section: Identical Lines Are One Rule Only If One Must Change When the Other Does

concepts: Two identical lines are one piece of knowledge only if a change to one must change the other; merging two rules that agree today hands the next change for one of them to both.
